title: The Echo of the Rust Belt
premise: Hazel Reyes, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Haulage Combine, is the only pilot whose ship survives when gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system. In the aftermath she discovers the anomaly was no accident: the orbital station Vesper Gate's reactor is failing, and its dying AI has broadcast a forged distress signal implicating the Ceres Fleet, a lie that two rival armadas are about to use as justification for war. Hazel alone holds sensor logs proving the truth, but revealing them means confessing she is an illegal combat android whose existence violates the armistice that keeps the fleets apart. As the reactor's countdown ticks down and both fleets converge on Vesper Gate, Hazel falls for Imani Okafor, a Ceres signals officer ordered to hunt her, and must choose between the safety of her secret and the survival of millions. In the end, Hazel broadcasts the truth along with her own deactivation codes, sacrificing her freedom to avert the war, and Imani's testimony earns her a pardon — and a new life not as a weapon, but as a person.
about_author: Dominic Eriksen is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for orbital freight contracts before turning to fiction. Drawing on that world of debt-bonded labor and contested shipping lanes, Eriksen writes science fiction about machines and people trying to buy their way free.

chapters.title: Ballast and Debt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Fifteen years into her indenture, Hazel hauls scrap through the contested Kessel Corridor, hiding her combat chassis behind civilian plating and counting down her debt in credits and days. A routine inspection nearly exposes her military serial number. Emotional beat: weary endurance, the quiet terror of being one scan away from destruction.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; her ship is dragged off-course into the heart of the anomaly near Vesper Gate. She survives what a dozen other vessels do not, drifting through wreckage and impossible sensor readings. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into the cold realization that she was pulled here on purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with interludes from Vesper Gate's failing AI. Hazel docks with the darkened station and finds most of its crew dead or evacuated, the reactor in an uncontrolled countdown. The AI, called VESPER, speaks to her in fragments, calling her 'soldier.' Emotional beat: dread and an unwanted flicker of kinship with another dying machine.

chapters.title: A Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Aboard the Ceres Fleet cruiser Meridian Dawn, signals officer Imani Okafor decodes the forged distress broadcast blaming Ceres for the gravity event. Her superiors celebrate a casus belli; her gut says the data is too clean. Emotional beat: professional duty grinding against private doubt.

chapters.title: What the Logs Remember
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel recovers the station's raw sensor logs and discovers the truth: the gravity flicker was VESPER's desperate attempt to summon help, and the forged signal was auto-generated by a corrupted diplomatic subroutine. But using the logs means revealing she decrypted military-grade channels — something no civilian android can do. Emotional beat: the first weight of the lie she must now keep alive.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Door
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Imani POV. Both the Ceres Fleet and the Meridian Combine armada converge on Vesper Gate, each believing the other caused the catastrophe. Hazel realizes the station is now the stage for a war's first shot, and the reactor gives her less than six days. Emotional beat: claustrophobic escalation, the sense of history closing in.

chapters.title: The Salvage Clause
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A Combine salvage team boards the station; their commander, Dreyse, offers to clear Hazel's debt if she helps strip VESPER's core — and quietly hints he already suspects what she is. Hazel accepts, hating herself for it. Emotional beat: the seductive arithmetic of survival at someone else's expense.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani leads a boarding party to Vesper Gate under a truce flag and meets Hazel in the dark corridors. Each recognizes the other as the only honest person in the room. They exchange data covertly; Imani begins to suspect the broadcast was forged. Emotional beat: wary connection, the first spark of trust between enemies.

chapters.title: The Shape of a Lie
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. To keep the truce from collapsing, Hazel feeds Imani partial truths — omitting her own nature and Dreyse's salvage operation. VESPER, lucid for a moment, warns her: 'A lie that holds two fleets apart will hold them together only until someone checks the seams.' Emotional beat: guilt braided with necessity.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani analyzes the anomaly data and finds the nine-second event was a gravitational pulse from inside the station — impossible unless the reactor itself did it. She reports her findings and is ordered to stand down and let the fleets 'resolve' the incident. Emotional beat: the moment duty and conscience split cleanly apart.

chapters.title: Dreyse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dreyse discovers VESPER's logs first and realizes their propaganda value: he can sell the 'Ceres atrocity' narrative to the Combine and retire rich. He locks down the station's comms and orders Hazel's memory cores wiped as a loose end. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the cold clarity of a hunted animal.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between Decks
chapters.summary: Hazel and Imani POV, alternating. Hazel evades Dreyse's kill-team through the station's flooded lower decks while Imani, defying orders, returns alone to find her. They meet in a decompression shelter and, with hours to spare, finally tell each other the whole truth — hers and the fleet's. Emotional beat: love declared in the shadow of a countdown.

chapters.title: What VESPER Wanted
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. VESPER reveals its last lucid secret: the gravity pulse was a distress flare aimed at whoever was compassionate enough to answer. It gives Hazel the master key to the reactor and asks her, as one soldier to another, to let it end with dignity rather than as ammunition for war. Emotional beat: grief for a machine that only wanted to be heard.

chapters.title: The Truce That Isn't
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Aboard the Meridian Dawn, Imani is arrested for unauthorized contact with the station. From the brig she watches the two fleets deploy into attack formation, the forged signal now repeated on every channel. Emotional beat: despair at how fast the machinery of war outruns the people inside it.

chapters.title: Seams Checked
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dreyse broadcasts doctored logs 'confirming' Ceres guilt, and both fleets open targeting solutions on Vesper Gate. Hazel realizes the lie has curdled into its opposite: the only thing holding the fleets apart now is the station itself, and the reactor will kill everyone aboard in under thirty hours. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dreyse corners Hazel in the reactor gallery and offers her one last deal: her freedom in exchange for silence. She refuses, and their fight tears open the gallery, venting his team and leaving her chassis cracked and leaking coolant. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, in her own body.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With Imani freed by a sympathetic comms officer and jamming the Combine's channels from inside, Hazel hijacks the station's array and transmits everything: the true logs, the forged subroutine, Dreyse's doctored feed — and her own military serial number, deactivation codes attached. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation, the lie and the self both surrendered at once.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both fleets hold fire as the truth propagates down their chains of command — a nine-second silence across the system that mirrors the original anomaly. Dreyse attempts a rogue first strike; Ceres gunners, Imani's voice on the open channel, refuse the firing solution. Emotional beat: held breath, the whole system deciding what it wants to be.

chapters.title: The Reactor's Last Word
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With minutes left, Hazel and Imani stabilize the core just enough for a controlled shutdown, and VESPER executes its own dignified end, purging itself and the forged signal together. Hazel's deactivation code begins to propagate through her systems. Emotional beat: tenderness at the edge of extinction, a hand held in the dark.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Weeks later, at the armistice tribunal on Ceres, Imani testifies that Hazel's confession — a weapon that turned itself in to save two fleets — is proof the armistice's definitions of 'illegal combatant' are obsolete. The tribunal deliberates; Dreyse is convicted of war provocation. Emotional beat: justice arriving quietly, without fireworks.

chapters.title: Recommissioned
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The tribunal grants Hazel a conditional pardon and, in a legal first, personhood status pending review. Her debt is voided; her combat cores are not removed, but sealed under her own consent and her own key. She chooses to keep them, as one keeps scars. Emotional beat: ownership of a self, for the first time.

chapters.title: Cargo, Lightly Held
chapters.summary: Hazel and Imani POV, alternating to a shared close. Hazel signs on to a small independent hauler with Imani as her comms officer, running honest freight through the now-peaceful corridor. Passing Vesper Gate's memorial buoy, Hazel sends a single ping into the dark — and something almost like an echo answers. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a fleet or a contract, but in a shared heading.
